name: Allergy & Sensitivity Guidance Catalog
purpose: Organizes DNA-linked allergy and atopy context beside exposure categories that require personal history or clinical testing.

display.title: Allergy & sensitivity map
display.subtitle: DNA signals worth matching to your history.
display.dna_intro: Matched variants in immune, skin-barrier, airway, and medication-sensitivity pathways.
display.exposure_intro: Record repeatable reactions to these exposures. They are not resolved by this consumer DNA file.
display.compact_footer: Use matched pathways to focus symptom, exposure, or medication review.

dna_contexts.label: Atopy & IgE tendency
dna_contexts.summary: Matched variants point to immune-response pathways seen in hay fever, asthma, eczema, and higher IgE.
dna_contexts.relevance: Most useful when seasonal allergies, wheeze, eczema, or elevated IgE/eosinophils fit your history.
dna_contexts.next_step: Compare with your symptom and exposure history; ask about IgE, eosinophils, or spirometry when symptoms fit.

dna_contexts.label: Skin barrier & eczema
dna_contexts.summary: Matched variants point to skin-barrier and type-2 immune pathways.
dna_contexts.relevance: Most useful when dry skin, recurrent eczema, itching, or barrier flares are part of your history.
dna_contexts.next_step: Track skin triggers and discuss dermatology or allergy review if flares are persistent or severe.

dna_contexts.label: Food-allergy research context
dna_contexts.summary: Matched variants overlap food-sensitization and skin-barrier pathways. The named foods are a tracking shortlist, not an automatic avoid list.
dna_contexts.relevance: Most useful when a repeatable reaction follows one of the listed foods or ingredients.
examples: fish such as salmon or cod
dna_contexts.next_step: Record the food, amount, timing, symptoms, and repeatability; use allergist-directed testing when the history fits.

dna_contexts.label: Inhalant & seasonal triggers
dna_contexts.summary: Matched variants overlap airway and seasonal-allergy pathways.
dna_contexts.relevance: Pollen, dust, mold, dander, or workplace exposures matter most when congestion, itchy eyes, cough, or wheeze follows them.
dna_contexts.next_step: Log location and timing with congestion, itchy eyes, cough, or wheeze; ask about targeted testing or spirometry if needed.

dna_contexts.label: Hives & mediator biology
dna_contexts.summary: Matched variants overlap mast-cell, hives, and mediator pathways.
dna_contexts.relevance: Most useful when episodes include hives, flushing, swelling, or reactions after heat, pressure, exercise, alcohol, or medicines.
examples: swelling of lips, face, or throat
reactions after heat, pressure, exercise, alcohol, or medicines
dna_contexts.next_step: Keep a dated episode log; discuss baseline or event tryptase and allergy/immunology review when clinically appropriate.

dna_contexts.label: Angioedema pathway
dna_contexts.summary: A matched panel points to a hereditary swelling pathway.
dna_contexts.relevance: Recurrent swelling without hives, abdominal attacks, or a family history makes this finding more important to discuss promptly.
dna_contexts.next_step: Discuss complement testing and specialist evaluation; urgent breathing or throat swelling needs emergency care.

clinical_safety_routes.label: Abacavir hypersensitivity
clinical_safety_routes.summary: If abacavir is considered, this matched signal is relevant to serious hypersensitivity risk.
clinical_safety_routes.relevance: Keep this finding with your medication record and show it before abacavir exposure.
clinical_safety_routes.next_step: Use validated clinical HLA testing and prescriber guidance before first exposure.

clinical_safety_routes.label: Carbamazepine / oxcarbazepine hypersensitivity
clinical_safety_routes.summary: If carbamazepine or oxcarbazepine is considered, this matched signal is relevant to severe skin-reaction risk.
clinical_safety_routes.relevance: Keep this finding visible before either medicine is started.
clinical_safety_routes.next_step: Confirm the relevant HLA alleles clinically before first exposure when the prescriber is considering these medicines.

clinical_safety_routes.label: Phenytoin hypersensitivity
clinical_safety_routes.summary: If phenytoin is considered, this matched signal is relevant to severe skin-reaction risk and medication exposure.
clinical_safety_routes.relevance: Keep this finding visible before phenytoin exposure and include the medication question in review.
clinical_safety_routes.next_step: Ask the prescriber about validated HLA/CYP2C9 review and serum-level monitoring before use.

clinical_safety_routes.label: Allopurinol hypersensitivity
clinical_safety_routes.summary: If allopurinol is considered, this matched signal is relevant to severe skin-reaction risk.
clinical_safety_routes.relevance: Keep this finding visible before allopurinol exposure.
clinical_safety_routes.next_step: Use validated clinical HLA testing and prescribing guidance before initiation.
